title: Torrey Pine: Ancient Torrey Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: Three Torrey pines on Coronado's heritage list, among them the city's Official Tree in Palm Park, all from a town-wide planting about a century ago.
intro: All three of our Torrey pines stand in Coronado, across the bay from downtown San Diego, and all three are on the city's official list of fifteen heritage trees. They come from one campaign. About a century ago Coronado planted Torrey pines across town under Louis C. Bandel, its Parks Superintendent for forty years, assisted, in the city's own words, by Kate Sessions. The one in Palm Park was recognised as the city's Official Tree in 2006 and became serial 001 on the heritage list in 2008. Serial 002 stands near the front doors of the public library, flanked by two Norfolk Island pines planted in 1909. Serial 004 has Cronan Park, a small triangle at Sixth Street and Pomona Avenue named for a sailor of the USS Bennington, almost to itself. The century is the city's round figure, and no planting year or measurement has been published for any of them.
